content:
watchOS 27 is coming soon, the next major software update for Apple Watch. I've been testing the watchOS 27 beta this summer, and there are three new features I particularly love.

#1: New home screen view

I don't think Apple has ever truly nailed the watchOS home screen. The original honeycomb design looks great in marketing images, and the list view added later has been my go-to, but both ways can feel a bit clunky.

The issue is that Apple Watch is designed for very brief micro-interactions. And watchOS comes preloaded with tons of apps—plus whatever third parties add—so scrolling through a bunch of apps you never use to find the one you want is a hassle.

watchOS 27 offers a solution: a dynamic app grid, the new default home screen view.

The dynamic app grid is similar to the honeycomb-style "grid view," but only shows your five most frequently used apps plus the Siri app. In my experience, it almost always includes the app I want to use. In the rare cases when it doesn't, you can still opt to bring up the full app view.

Most of the time, my watch face complications are my primary way to launch apps. But now the dynamic app grid serves as a handy secondary option.

#2: Tap gesture

Over the past few years, Apple has gradually introduced different interesting ways to interact with watchOS through gestures.

Double Tap was the first gesture introduced, and last year Wrist Flick was added.

Now in watchOS 27, there's a third option: Tap. It's similar to Double Tap, but it's just a single tap and only works with the Smart Stack.

When browsing the Smart Stack, just tap with your index finger and thumb once, and it'll select the highlighted widget. Basically, it's a handy selection tool.

Now you can open the Smart Stack, navigate with Double Tap, then use the new Tap gesture to select a widget to open the corresponding app.

#3: Siri AI

Siri AI is at the core of all Apple's new software this fall, and watchOS 27 is no exception.

Apple rebuilt Siri from the ground up for the AI era—a major upgrade from before.

watchOS 27 adds a dedicated Siri app, where you can browse all your conversations with the Siri assistant across all your devices. Importantly, the Apple Watch version of Siri is absolutely not a stripped-down or feature-poor wrist version. It's exactly the same Siri AI you'd find on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and so on.

According to Apple's senior director of watchOS software engineering (via TechRadar), this is one of the goals of the Siri overhaul:

While a few other companies are trying to build successful AI wearables, with the launch of watchOS 27, the already hugely popular Apple Watch is going to be one of them.

What features of watchOS 27 do you like? Let us know in the comments.
